sentences.text: Pteraspis was an extinct genus of jawless fish belonging to the heterostracan group.
This creature possessed protective armor plating on its front body and lacked fins except for a lobed tail.
It featured two wing-like protrusions over its gills and a single protrusion on its back, derived from armored plates.
Pteraspis had stiff spines on its back, which may have served as protection against predators.
The largest recorded specimens of Pteraspis reached an estimated length of 27 cm.
The genus Pteraspis was described by Kner in 1847.
Pteraspis likely fed on shoals of plankton just beneath the ocean surface.
The wing-like protrusions and horn-like rostrum of Pteraspis suggest it had good swimming ability.
The type species for the genus Pteraspis is Cephalaspis rostrata.
Known species of Pteraspis include P. rostrata, P. dunensis, and P. crouchi.
Pteraspis is classified within the class Pteraspidomorphi.
Pteraspis belongs to the family Pteraspididae.
Pteraspis lived during the Lochkovian to Eifelian epochs of the Devonian period in regions now known as the Americas and Europe.
Fossil records of Pteraspis are found in both marine and freshwater environments.
Pteraspis lived from 419.62 to 387.95 million years ago during the Lochkovian to Eifelian stages.
